translations.literal: In the autumn of the eleventh year the Emperor again added three Vice Directors including Mo Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eleventh year the Emperor again added three Vice Directors including Mo Ying.

sentences.zh: 經上疏力爭，帝以已遣不聽。

translations.literal: Jing submitted a memorial arguing forcefully; the Emperor, having already dispatched them, would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jing submitted a memorial arguing forcefully, but the Emperor, having already dispatched them, would not listen.

sentences.zh: 內靈臺請錦衣余丁百人供灑掃，經等諫，不納。

translations.literal: The Inner Observatory requested a hundred surplus men from the Embroidered Guard for sweeping and cleaning; Jing and others remonstrated, but it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Observatory requested a hundred surplus men from the Embroidered Guard for sweeping and cleaning; Zhou Jing and others remonstrated, but the request was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 經曰：「祖宗設內臺，其地至密。

translations.literal: Jing said: "The founding emperors established the inner observatory in a place of utmost secrecy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jing said, "The founding emperors established the inner observatory in a place of utmost secrecy.

sentences.zh: 今一旦增百人，將必有漏泄妄言者。」

translations.literal: Now to add a hundred men at once will surely mean leaks and reckless talk.
translations.idiomatic: Now to add a hundred men at once will surely mean leaks and reckless talk.

sentences.zh: 帝悟，立已之。

translations.literal: The Emperor understood and immediately stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor understood and immediately stopped it.

sentences.zh: 崇王見澤乞河南退灘地二十餘里，經言不宜予。

translations.literal: Prince Chong Jian Ze requested more than twenty li of retreating shoal land in Henan; Jing said it should not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chong Jian Ze requested more than twenty li of retreating shoal land in Henan; Zhou Jing said it should not be granted.

sentences.zh: 興王祐杬前後乞赤馬諸河泊所及近湖地千三百余頃，經三疏爭之，竟不許。

translations.literal: Prince Xing You Yuan repeatedly requested the Chi Ma and other river port offices and nearby lake land totaling more than thirteen hundred qing; Jing argued in three memorials and in the end it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xing You Yuan repeatedly requested the Chi Ma and other river port offices and nearby lake land totaling more than thirteen hundred qing; Zhou Jing argued in three memorials, and in the end it was not granted.

sentences.zh: 帝以肅寧諸縣地四百余頃賜壽寧侯張鶴齡，其家人因侵民地三倍，且毆民至死，下巡撫高銓勘報。

translations.literal: The Emperor granted more than four hundred qing of land in Suining and other counties to Marquis of Shouning Zhang Heling; his household thereafter encroached on commoners' land to three times the amount and even beat a man to death; the matter was referred to Grand Coordinator Gao Quan for investigation and report.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor granted more than four hundred qing of land in Suining and other counties to Zhang Heling, Marquis of Shouning; his household thereafter encroached on commoners' land to three times the amount and even beat a man to death, and the matter was referred to Grand Coordinator Gao Quan for investigation and report.

sentences.zh: 銓言可耕者無幾，請仍賦民，不許。

translations.literal: Quan said arable land was negligible and requested that taxation still be assigned to the people; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Quan said arable land was negligible and requested that taxation still be assigned to the people, but this was not granted.

sentences.zh: 時王府、勛戚莊田例畝征銀三分，獨鶴齡奏加征二分，且概加之沙堿地。

translations.literal: At the time princely establishments and meritorious kin estates were taxed at three fen of silver per mu by precedent; Heling alone memorialized for an additional two fen, and even applied it wholesale to sandy and saline land.
translations.idiomatic: At the time princely establishments and meritorious kin estates were taxed at three fen of silver per mu by precedent; Heling alone memorialized for an additional two fen, and even applied it wholesale to sandy and saline land.

sentences.zh: 經抗章執奏，命侍郎許進偕太監朱秀覆核。

translations.literal: Jing submitted a defiant memorial and held fast; the Vice Minister Xu Jin was ordered together with Eunuch Zhu Xiu to re-examine the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jing submitted a defiant memorial and held fast; Vice Minister Xu Jin was ordered together with Eunuch Zhu Xiu to re-examine the matter.

sentences.zh: 經言：「地已再勘，今復遣使，徒滋煩擾。

translations.literal: Jing said: "The land has already been surveyed twice; to dispatch envoys again would only multiply vexation and disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jing said, "The land has already been surveyed twice; to dispatch envoys again would only multiply vexation and disturbance.

sentences.zh: 昔太祖以劉基故減青田賦，征米五合，欲使基鄉里子孫世世頌基。

translations.literal: Formerly the Taizu, because of Liu Ji, reduced Qingtian's tax levy to five he of grain, wishing Liu Ji's home village and descendants to praise Ji generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Taizu, because of Liu Ji, reduced Qingtian's tax levy to five he of grain, wishing Liu Ji's home village and descendants to praise Ji generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 今興濟篤生皇后，正宜恤民減賦，俾世世戴德，何乃使小民銜怨無已也。」

translations.literal: Now Xingji gave birth to the empress; this is precisely the time to show compassion to the people and reduce taxes, so that generation after generation they might bear gratitude—why instead make common folk bear endless resentment?
translations.idiomatic: Now Xingji gave birth to the empress; this is precisely the time to show compassion to the people and reduce taxes, so that generation after generation they might bear gratitude—why instead make common folk bear endless resentment?

sentences.zh: 頃之，進等還言此地乃憲廟皇親柏權及民恒產，不可奪。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Jin and the others returned saying this land was the regular property of the maternal kinsman Bai Quan under the Xian Emperor and of the people—it could not be seized.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter Xu Jin and the others returned saying this land was the regular property of the maternal kinsman Bai Quan under the Xian Emperor and of the people, and could not be seized.

sentences.zh: 帝竟予鶴齡，如其請加稅，而命償權直，除民租額。

translations.literal: The Emperor in the end granted it to Heling, added tax as he requested, and ordered compensation paid to Quan while excusing the people's rent quota.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor in the end granted it to Heling, added tax as he requested, and ordered compensation paid to Quan while excusing the people's rent quota.

sentences.zh: 經等復諫曰：「東宮、親王莊田征稅自有例，鶴齡不宜獨優。

translations.literal: Jing and others remonstrated again: "Eastern Palace and princely estate taxation has its own precedents; Heling should not alone receive preferential treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jing and others remonstrated again: "Eastern Palace and princely estate taxation has its own precedents; Heling should not alone receive preferential treatment.

sentences.zh: 權先帝妃家，亦戚畹也，名雖償直，實乃奪之。

translations.literal: Quan is of the former emperor's consort's family—also imperial kin; though nominally compensated, this is in fact seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Quan is of the former emperor's consort's family—also imperial kin; though nominally compensated, this is in fact seizure.

sentences.zh: 天下將謂陛下惟厚椒房親，不念先朝外戚。」

translations.literal: The realm will say Your Majesty favors only empress's kin and does not remember the maternal kin of the previous reign.
translations.idiomatic: The realm will say Your Majesty favors only the empress's kin and does not remember the maternal kin of the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 帝終不納。

translations.literal: The Emperor ultimately did not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ultimately did not accept this.

sentences.zh: 大同缺戰馬，馬文升請太倉銀以市。

translations.literal: Datong lacked war horses; Ma Wensheng requested Grand Granary silver to purchase them.
translations.idiomatic: Datong lacked war horses; Ma Wensheng requested Grand Granary silver to purchase them.

sentences.zh: 經言：「糧馬各有司存。

translations.literal: Jing said: "Grain and horses each have their responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jing said, "Grain and horses each have their responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 祖訓六部毋相壓，兵部侵戶部權，非祖訓。」

translations.literal: The ancestral instructions forbid the six ministries from overriding one another; for the Ministry of War to encroach on the Ministry of Revenue's authority is contrary to the ancestral instructions.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral instructions forbid the six ministries from overriding one another; for the Ministry of War to encroach on the Ministry of Revenue's authority is contrary to the ancestral instructions.

sentences.zh: 帝為改撥太僕銀給之。

translations.literal: The Emperor therefore redirected funds from the Court of the Imperial Stud to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor therefore redirected funds from the Court of the Imperial Stud to supply them.

sentences.zh: 給事中魯昂請盡括稅役金錢輸太倉，經曰：「不節織造、賞賚、齋醮、土木之費，而欲括天下財，是舛也。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Lu Ang requested that all tax and corvée money be swept into the Grand Granary; Jing said: "Without curbing expenditure on weaving, rewards, fasting rituals, and construction, yet wishing to sweep up the realm's wealth—this is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Lu Ang requested that all tax and corvée money be swept into the Grand Granary; Zhou Jing said, "Without curbing expenditure on weaving, rewards, fasting rituals, and construction, yet wishing to sweep up the realm's wealth—this is wrong.

sentences.zh: 內官傳旨索太倉銀三萬兩為燈費，持不與。

translations.literal: Eunuchs transmitted an edict demanding thirty thousand taels of Grand Granary silver for lantern expenses; he steadfastly refused to give them.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs transmitted an edict demanding thirty thousand taels of Grand Granary silver for lantern expenses; he steadfastly refused to give them.

sentences.zh: 經剛介方正，好強諫，雖重忤旨不恤。

translations.literal: Jing was stern, upright, and square; he loved forceful remonstrance and even when he seriously defied the imperial will did not care.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jing was stern, upright, and square; he loved forceful remonstrance and even when he seriously defied the imperial will did not care.

sentences.zh: 宦官、貴戚皆憚而疾之。

translations.literal: Eunuchs and noble kin all feared and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs and noble kin all feared and hated him.

sentences.zh: 太監李廣死，帝得朝臣與饋遺簿籍，大怒。

translations.literal: When Eunuch Director Li Guang died, the Emperor obtained the ledgers of court ministers' gifts and presents and was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: When Eunuch Director Li Guang died, the Emperor obtained the ledgers of court ministers' gifts and presents and was greatly angered.

sentences.zh: 科道因劾諸臣交通狀，有及經者。

translations.literal: The censorate and remonstrance officials therefore impeached ministers for collusion; Jing was among those named.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate and remonstrance officials therefore impeached ministers for collusion, and Zhou Jing was among those named.

sentences.zh: 經上疏曰：「昨科道劾廷臣奔競李廣，闌入臣名。

translations.literal: Jing submitted a memorial saying: "Yesterday the censorate impeached court ministers for scrambling after Li Guang, and my name was inserted among them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jing submitted a memorial saying, "Yesterday the censorate impeached court ministers for scrambling after Li Guang, and my name was inserted among them.

sentences.zh: 雖蒙恩不問，實含傷忍痛，無以自明。

translations.literal: Though favored with the grace of no inquiry, in truth I have swallowed injury and borne pain, with no way to clear myself.
translations.idiomatic: Though favored with the grace of no inquiry, in truth I have swallowed injury and borne pain, with no way to clear myself.

sentences.zh: 夫人奔競李廣，冀其進言左右，圖寵眷耳。

translations.literal: Men scrambled after Li Guang hoping he would speak for them at the emperor's side and seek favor and regard.
translations.idiomatic: Men scrambled after Li Guang hoping he would speak for them at the emperor's side and seek favor and regard.

sentences.zh: 陛下試思廣在時，曾言及臣否。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should consider: when Guang was alive, did he ever speak of me?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should consider: when Guang was alive, did he ever speak of me?

sentences.zh: 且交結饋遺簿籍具在，乞檢曾否有臣姓名。

translations.literal: Moreover, the ledgers of collusion and gifts still exist; I beg that they be checked for whether my name ever appears.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the ledgers of collusion and gifts still exist; I beg that they be checked for whether my name ever appears.

sentences.zh: 更嚴鞫廣家人，臣但有寸金、尺帛，即治臣交結之罪，斬首市曹，以為奔競無恥之戒。

translations.literal: Further, interrogate Guang's household strictly—if I possessed so much as an inch of gold or a foot of silk, then punish me for collusion, behead me in the marketplace as a warning against shameless scrambling.
translations.idiomatic: Further, interrogate Guang's household strictly—if I possessed so much as an inch of gold or a foot of silk, then punish me for collusion and behead me in the marketplace as a warning against shameless scrambling.

sentences.zh: 若無幹涉，亦乞為臣洗雪，庶得展布四體，終事聖明。

translations.literal: If there is no involvement, I also beg that I be cleared, so that I may freely use my limbs and serve the sage brightness to the end.
translations.idiomatic: If there is no involvement, I also beg that I be cleared, so that I may freely use my limbs and serve Your Majesty to the end.

sentences.zh: 若令含汙忍垢，即死填溝壑，目且不瞑。」

translations.literal: If I am made to swallow filth and endure stain, even in death filling a ditch and gully my eyes would not close.
translations.idiomatic: If I am made to swallow filth and endure stain, even in death filling a ditch and gully my eyes would not close.

sentences.zh: 帝慰答之。

translations.literal: The Emperor comforted him with a reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor comforted him with a reply.

sentences.zh: 十三年，星變，自陳乞休。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, with an alteration in the stars, he memorialized on his own behalf begging to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, with an alteration in the stars, he memorialized on his own behalf begging to retire.

sentences.zh: 報許，賜敕馳驛，加太子太保，以侶鐘代。

translations.literal: The reply granted his request; he was given an edict and post horses, promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Lü Zhong replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: The reply granted his request; he was given an edict and post horses, promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Lü Zhong replaced him.

sentences.zh: 廷臣爭上章留之，中外論薦者至八十余疏，鹹報寢。

translations.literal: Court ministers vied to submit memorials asking him to stay; inside and outside the court more than eighty memorials recommending him arrived—all were left without response.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers vied to submit memorials asking him to stay; inside and outside the court more than eighty memorials recommending him arrived—all were left without response.

sentences.zh: 子曾，進士。

translations.literal: His son Zeng was a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zeng was a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 浙江右參政。

translations.literal: Right Assistant Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Right Assistant Commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 耿裕，字好問，刑部尚書九疇子也。

translations.literal: Geng Yu, styled Haowen, was the son of Minister of Punishments Jiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Yu, whose style name was Haowen, was the son of Minister of Punishments Jiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Jingtai.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授戶科給事中，改工科。

translations.literal: He was changed to a Hanlin bachelor, appointed Supervising Secretary in the Revenue Section, then transferred to the Works Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to a Hanlin bachelor, appointed Supervising Secretary in the Revenue Section, then transferred to the Works Section.

sentences.zh: 天順初，以九疇為右都御史，改裕檢討。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun, because Jiuzhou became Censor-in-Chief of the Right, Yu was transferred to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianshun, because Jiuzhou became Censor-in-Chief of the Right, Yu was transferred to Compiler.

sentences.zh: 九疇坐劾石亨貶，裕亦謫泗州判官。

translations.literal: Jiuzhou was demoted for impeaching Shi Heng; Yu was also banished as assistant magistrate of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuzhou was demoted for impeaching Shi Heng; Yu was also banished as assistant magistrate of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 終父喪，補定州。

translations.literal: After completing mourning for his father, he was reassigned to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his father, he was reassigned to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 成化初，召復檢討，歷國子司業、祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he was recalled as Compiler and served successively as Vice Director and Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chenghua he was recalled as Compiler and served successively as Vice Director and Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 侯伯年幼者皆肄業監中，裕采古諸侯、貴戚言行可法者為書授之，帝聞而稱善。

translations.literal: Young marquises and earls all studied at the directorate; Yu compiled a book of the conduct and words of ancient feudal lords and noble kin worthy of emulation and taught from it; the Emperor heard of this and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Young marquises and earls all studied at the directorate; Yu compiled a book of the conduct and words of ancient feudal lords and noble kin worthy of emulation and taught from it, and the Emperor heard of this and praised it.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部左右侍郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as Left and Right Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Left and Right Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 坐尚書尹旻累，停俸者再。

translations.literal: Because of Minister Yin Min's setbacks he was punished twice with suspension of salary.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Minister Yin Min's setbacks he was punished twice with suspension of salary.

sentences.zh: 已，代旻為尚書。

translations.literal: Thereafter he replaced Min as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he replaced Yin Min as Minister.

sentences.zh: 大學士萬安與裕不協，而李孜省私其同鄉李裕，欲使代裕，相與謀中之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wan An was at odds with Yu, and Li Zisheng favored his fellow townsman Li Yu and wished to have him replace Yu; together they plotted to bring Yu down.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wan An was at odds with Yu, and Li Zisheng favored his fellow townsman Li Yu and wished to have him replace Yu; together they plotted to bring Yu down.

sentences.zh: 坐以事，調侍郎黎淳南京，而奪裕俸。

translations.literal: On a charge of misconduct, Vice Minister Li Chun was transferred to Nanjing and Yu's salary was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: On a charge of misconduct, Vice Minister Li Chun was transferred to Nanjing and Yu's salary was stripped.

sentences.zh: 言官復交劾，宥之。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials again impeached him in succession; he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials again impeached him in succession, but he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 裕入謝，既出，帝怒曰：「吾再寬裕罪，當再謝。

translations.literal: Yu entered to give thanks; after he left, the Emperor angrily said: "I have twice pardoned Yu's offenses; he ought to thank me twice.
translations.idiomatic: Yu entered to give thanks; after he left, the Emperor angrily said, "I have twice pardoned Yu's offenses; he ought to thank me twice.

sentences.zh: 今一謝，以奪俸故，意鞅鞅耶？」

translations.literal: Now he thanks once—is he discontented because his salary was taken?
translations.idiomatic: Now he thanks once—is he discontented because his salary was taken?

sentences.zh: 孜省等因而傾之，遂調南京禮部，而以李裕代。

translations.literal: Zisheng and the others therefore toppled him; he was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of Rites and Li Yu replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Zisheng and the others therefore toppled him; he was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of Rites and Li Yu replaced him.

sentences.zh: 逾年，孝宗嗣位，轉南京兵部參贊機務。

translations.literal: A year later, when the Hongzhi Emperor succeeded, he was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of War to assist in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, when the Hongzhi Emperor succeeded, he was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of War to assist in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 弘治改元，召拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Hongzhi's reign began, he was summoned and appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzhi's reign began, he was summoned and appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時公私侈靡，耗費日廣。

translations.literal: At the time public and private life were extravagant and wasteful, and expenditure grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: At the time public and private life were extravagant and wasteful, and expenditure grew daily.

sentences.zh: 裕隨事救正，因災異條上時事及申理言官，先後陳言甚眾，大要歸於節儉。

translations.literal: Yu corrected matters as they arose; in response to portents he itemized current affairs and vindicated remonstrance officials; he spoke out on many matters in succession, all in essence returning to thrift.
translations.idiomatic: Yu corrected matters as they arose; in response to portents he itemized current affairs and vindicated remonstrance officials; he spoke out on many matters in succession, all in essence returning to thrift.

sentences.zh: 給事中鄭宗仁疏節光祿供應，裕等請納其奏。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zheng Zongren memorialized to trim the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' provisions; Yu and others asked that his memorial be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zheng Zongren memorialized to trim the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' provisions; Yu and others asked that his memorial be accepted.

sentences.zh: 巡視光祿御史田{大淵}以供費不足累行戶，請借太倉銀償之。

translations.literal: Censor Tian Dayuan, inspecting the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, said provisioning costs were insufficient and burdened traveling households; he requested borrowing Grand Granary silver to compensate them.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Tian Dayuan, inspecting the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, said provisioning costs were insufficient and burdened traveling households; he requested borrowing Grand Granary silver to compensate them.

sentences.zh: 裕等言，疑有侵盜弊，請敕所司禁防，帝皆從之。

translations.literal: Yu and others said they suspected corruption of embezzlement and asked that the responsible offices be ordered to forbid and guard against it; the Emperor accepted all of this.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and others said they suspected embezzlement and asked that the responsible offices be ordered to forbid and guard against it; the Emperor accepted all of this.

sentences.zh: 南京守備中官請增奉先殿日供品物，裕等不可。

translations.literal: The Nanjing defender eunuch requested to increase the daily offerings at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors; Yu and the others did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanjing defender eunuch requested an increase in the daily offerings at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors, but Yu and the others refused.

sentences.zh: 帝方踐阼，斥番僧還本土，止留乳奴班丹等十五人。

translations.literal: The Emperor had just ascended the throne; he expelled Tibetan monks back to their native lands, keeping only fifteen including Runu Bandan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had just taken the throne. He expelled the Tibetan monks to their homelands, keeping only fifteen, including Runu Bandan.

sentences.zh: 其後多潛匿京師，轉相招引，齋醮復興。

translations.literal: Afterward many secretly hid in the capital, inviting one another in turn, and Buddhist rites revived.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward many secretly remained in the capital, inviting one another, and Buddhist rites flourished again.

sentences.zh: 言官以為言，裕等因力請驅斥。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials raised the matter; Yu and the others therefore strongly petitioned for their expulsion.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials raised the matter, and Yu and the others therefore strongly petitioned for their expulsion.

sentences.zh: 帝乃留百八十二人，余悉逐之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then kept one hundred eighty-two and expelled all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then kept one hundred eighty-two and expelled all the rest.

sentences.zh: 禮部公廨火，裕及侍郎倪嶽、周經等請罪，被劾下獄。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites office building caught fire; Yu and Vice Ministers Ni Yue, Zhou Jing, and others submitted guilty pleas and were impeached and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Rites office caught fire, Yu and Vice Ministers Ni Yue, Zhou Jing, and others submitted guilty pleas and were impeached and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 已，釋之，停其俸。

translations.literal: Soon after they were released, but their salaries were suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they were released, but their salaries were suspended.

sentences.zh: 初，撒馬兒罕及土魯番皆貢獅子，甘肅鎮守太監傅德先圖形以進，巡按御史陳瑤請卻之。

translations.literal: At first Samarkand and Turfan both presented lions; Fu De, the eunuch defending Gansu, had illustrations made and presented them; Regional Inspector Chen Yao asked to reject them.
translations.idiomatic: At first Samarkand and Turfan both sent lions as tribute. Fu De, the eunuch defending Gansu, had illustrations made and presented them, but Regional Inspector Chen Yao asked that they be refused.

sentences.zh: 裕等乞從瑤請，而治德違詔罪，帝不從。

translations.literal: Yu and the others begged to follow Chen Yao's request and punish De for violating the edict; the Emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and the others asked to follow Chen Yao's request and punish De for violating the edict, but the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 後番使再至，留京師，頻有宣召。

translations.literal: Later the foreign envoys came again, stayed in the capital, and were frequently summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Later the foreign envoys came again, remained in the capital, and were frequently summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 裕等言：「番人不道，因朝貢許其自新。

translations.literal: Yu and the others said: "The foreigners are unprincipled; because of their tribute we allowed them to reform.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and the others said, "The foreigners are unprincipled. Because they sent tribute, we allowed them to reform.

sentences.zh: 彼復潛稱可汗，興兵犯順。

translations.literal: They again secretly styled themselves khans and raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: They again secretly styled themselves khans and raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 陛下優假其使，適遇倔強之時，彼將謂天朝畏之，益長桀驁。

translations.literal: Your Majesty favors and indulges their envoys at just the time they are defiant; they will think the Celestial Court fears them and grow more rebellious and arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty favors and indulges their envoys at just the moment they are defiant. They will think the Celestial Court fears them and grow ever more rebellious and arrogant.

sentences.zh: 且獅子野獸，無足珍異。」

translations.literal: Moreover lions are wild beasts, scarcely worthy of wonder."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, lions are wild beasts, scarcely worthy of wonder."

sentences.zh: 帝即遣其使還。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately sent their envoys back.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor immediately sent their envoys back.

sentences.zh: 尋代王恕為吏部尚書，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Wang Shu as Minister of Personnel and was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he replaced Wang Shu as Minister of Personnel and was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 禦用監匠人李綸等以內降得官，裕言：「先有詔，文官不由臣部推舉傳乞除授者，參送法司按治。

translations.literal: Artisans of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactures such as Li Lun received appointments by inner decree; Yu said: "There was already an edict that civil officials not recommended by our ministry but appointed through solicitation should be referred to the judicial authorities for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Artisans of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactures such as Li Lun received appointments by inner decree. Yu said, "There was already an edict that civil officials not recommended by our ministry but appointed through solicitation should be referred to the judicial authorities for investigation.

sentences.zh: 今除用綸等，不信前詔，不可。」

translations.literal: Now appointing Lun and the others disregards the earlier edict and is impermissible."
translations.idiomatic: Now appointing Lun and the others disregards the earlier edict and is impermissible."

sentences.zh: 給事中呂獻等皆論奏，裕亦再疏爭，終不聽。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries such as Lü Xian all submitted memorials; Yu also memorialized twice in dispute, but in the end the Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries such as Lü Xian all submitted memorials, and Yu also memorialized twice in protest, but in the end the Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 裕為人坦夷諒直，諳習朝章。

translations.literal: Yu was open, upright, and sincere by nature, well versed in court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was open, upright, and sincere by nature, and well versed in court regulations.

sentences.zh: 秉銓數年，無愛憎，亦不徇毀譽，銓政稱平。

translations.literal: Holding the selection office for several years, he had no favorites or hatreds and did not yield to praise or blame; personnel administration was called fair.
translations.idiomatic: He held the selection office for several years without favor or hatred, and did not yield to praise or blame. Personnel administration was called fair.

sentences.zh: 自奉淡泊。

translations.literal: He lived plainly himself.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly himself.

sentences.zh: 兩世貴盛，而家業蕭然，父子並以名德稱。

translations.literal: Though noble and prosperous for two generations, the family holdings were sparse; father and son were both renowned for integrity and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Though noble and prosperous for two generations, the family's holdings were sparse, and father and son were both renowned for integrity and virtue.

sentences.zh: 九年正月卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year he died, aged sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，謚文恪。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Mentor and given the posthumous title Wenge.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Mentor and given the posthumous title Wenge.

sentences.zh: 倪嶽，字舜咨，上元人。

translations.literal: Ni Yue, styled Shunzi, was a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Yue, styled Shunzi, was a native of Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 父謙，奉命祀北嶽，母夢緋衣神入室，生嶽，遂以為名。

translations.literal: His father Qian, while ordered to perform sacrifices at the Northern Peak, dreamed that a deity in crimson robes entered the chamber; when Yue was born he was so named.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian, while ordered to perform sacrifices at the Northern Peak, dreamed that a deity in crimson robes entered the chamber. When Yue was born, he was so named.

sentences.zh: 謙終南京禮部尚書，謚文僖。

translations.literal: Qian ended as Minister of Rites at Nanjing and was given the posthumous title Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qian ended his career as Minister of Rites at Nanjing and was given the posthumous title Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 嶽，天順八年進士。

translations.literal: Yue passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: Yue passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor and appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor and appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 成化中，歷侍讀學士，直講東宮。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign he served as Reader-in-waiting and lectured in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign he served as Reader-in-waiting and lectured in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 二十二年擢禮部右侍郎，仍直經筵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites of the right and continued at the Classics Lectern.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites of the right and continued at the Classics Lectern.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，改左侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was transferred to Vice Minister of the left.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was transferred to Vice Minister of the left.

sentences.zh: 嶽好學，文章敏捷，博綜經世之務。

translations.literal: Yue loved learning; his writing was quick, and he broadly mastered affairs of statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Yue loved learning. His writing was quick, and he broadly mastered affairs of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 尚書耿裕方正持大體，至禮文制度率待嶽而決。

translations.literal: Minister Geng Yu was upright and held to broad principles; in rites, documents, and regulations he generally waited for Yue to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Geng Yu was upright and held to broad principles. In rites, documents, and regulations he generally waited for Yue to decide.

sentences.zh: 六年，裕改吏部，嶽遂代為尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Yu transferred to Personnel; Yue then replaced him as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Yu transferred to Personnel, and Yue then replaced him as Minister.

sentences.zh: 詔召國師領占竹於四川，嶽力諫，帝不從。

translations.literal: An edict summoned the State Preceptor Lingzhanzhu to Sichuan; Yue strongly remonstrated, but the Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned the State Preceptor Lingzhanzhu to Sichuan. Yue strongly remonstrated, but the Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 給事中夏昂、御史張禎等相繼爭之，事竟寢。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Xia Ang, Censor Zhang Zhen, and others protested in succession; the matter was finally dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Xia Ang, Censor Zhang Zhen, and others protested in succession, and the matter was finally dropped.

sentences.zh: 時營造諸王府，規制宏麗，逾永樂、宣德之舊。

translations.literal: At the time construction of princely residences was on a grand and sumptuous scale, exceeding the Yongle and Xuande standards.
translations.idiomatic: At the time construction of princely residences was on a grand and sumptuous scale, exceeding the standards of the Yongle and Xuande reigns.

sentences.zh: 嶽請頒成式。

translations.literal: Yue asked that fixed standards be promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: Yue asked that fixed standards be promulgated.

sentences.zh: 又以四方所報災異，禮部於歲終類奏，率為具文，乃詳次其月日，博引經史征應。

translations.literal: He also noted that in the memorials on calamities and portents reported from all quarters, the Ministry of Rites at year's end submitted classified summaries that were usually empty forms; he therefore arranged them in detail by month and day and broadly cited classics and histories for corroborating signs.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that when calamities and portents were reported from all quarters, the Ministry of Rites at year's end submitted classified summaries that were usually empty forms. He therefore arranged them in detail by month and day and broadly cited classics and histories for corroborating signs.

sentences.zh: 勸帝勤講學，開言路，寬賦役，慎刑罰，黜奸貪，進忠直，汰冗員，停齋醮，省營造，止濫賞。

translations.literal: He urged the Emperor to study diligently, open channels of remonstrance, lighten taxes and corvée, be cautious in punishments, dismiss the wicked and greedy, advance the loyal and upright, eliminate redundant officials, halt Buddhist rites, reduce construction, and stop indiscriminate rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the Emperor to study diligently, open channels of remonstrance, lighten taxes and corvée, be cautious in punishments, dismiss the wicked and greedy, advance the loyal and upright, eliminate redundant officials, halt Buddhist rites, reduce construction, and stop indiscriminate rewards.

sentences.zh: 帝頗采納焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor adopted much of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor adopted much of this.

sentences.zh: 左侍郎徐瓊與後家有連，謀代嶽。

translations.literal: Left Vice Minister Xu Qiong was connected to the empress's family and plotted to replace Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Minister Xu Qiong was connected to the empress's family and plotted to replace Yue.

sentences.zh: 九年，南京吏部缺尚書，廷推瓊。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel lacked a minister; the court recommended Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel lacked a minister, and the court recommended Qiong.

sentences.zh: 詔加嶽太子太保，往任之，而瓊果代嶽。

translations.literal: An edict added Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent to Yue and sent him to take the post; Qiong did indeed replace Yue.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent to Yue and sent him to take the post, while Qiong did indeed replace Yue.

sentences.zh: 尋改嶽南京兵部參贊機務。

translations.literal: Soon Yue was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of War as Coordinator of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yue was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of War as Coordinator of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 還，代屠滽為吏部尚書，嚴絕請托，不徇名譽，銓政稱平。

translations.literal: Returning, he replaced Tu Shu as Minister of Personnel, strictly refusing solicitations and not yielding to reputation; personnel administration was called fair.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he replaced Tu Shu as Minister of Personnel, strictly refusing solicitations and not yielding to reputation. Personnel administration was called fair.

sentences.zh: 嶽狀貌魁岸，風采嚴峻，善斷大事。

translations.literal: Yue was imposing in stature and stern in bearing, skilled at deciding great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was imposing in stature and stern in bearing, and skilled at deciding great affairs.

sentences.zh: 每盈廷聚議，決以片言，聞者悅服。

translations.literal: Whenever the full court gathered in deliberation, he decided matters in a few words, and those who heard were pleased and convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the full court gathered in deliberation, he decided matters in a few words, and those who heard were pleased and convinced.

sentences.zh: 同列中，最推遜馬文升，然論事未嘗茍同。

translations.literal: Among his colleagues he most deferred to Ma Wensheng, yet in discussing affairs he never agreed rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Among his colleagues he most deferred to Ma Wensheng, yet in discussing affairs he never agreed rashly.

sentences.zh: 前後陳請百余事，軍國弊政剔抉無遺。

translations.literal: Before and after he presented more than a hundred petitions, exposing every abuse in military and state affairs without omission.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after he presented more than a hundred petitions, exposing every abuse in military and state affairs without omission.

sentences.zh: 疏出，人多傳錄之。

translations.literal: When his memorials appeared, many copied and circulated them.
translations.idiomatic: When his memorials appeared, many copied and circulated them.

sentences.zh: 論西北用兵害尤切，其略云：

translations.literal: His discussion of the harm of employing troops in the northwest was especially urgent; the gist ran:
translations.idiomatic: His discussion of the harm of employing troops in the northwest was especially urgent. The gist ran:

sentences.zh: 近歲毛裏孩、阿羅忽、孛羅出、乚加思蘭大為邊患。

translations.literal: In recent years Molihai, Aluohu, Boluochu, and Bekzadaslan have greatly troubled the borders.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years Molihai, Aluohu, Boluochu, and Bekzadaslan have greatly troubled the borders.

sentences.zh: 蓋緣河套之中，水草甘肥，易於屯牧，故賊頻據彼地，擁眾入掠。

translations.literal: This is because within the Ordos Loop the grass and water are sweet and rich, easy for encampment and pasture; therefore the bandits frequently occupy that region and lead crowds in raids.
translations.idiomatic: This is because within the Ordos Loop the grass and water are sweet and rich, easy for encampment and pasture. The bandits therefore frequently occupy that region and lead crowds in raids.

sentences.zh: 諸將怯懦，率嬰城自守。

translations.literal: The generals are timid and cowardly, mostly locking themselves inside walled cities.
translations.idiomatic: The generals are timid and cowardly, mostly locking themselves inside walled cities.

sentences.zh: 茍或遇敵，輒至挫衄。

translations.literal: If they happen to meet the enemy, they immediately suffer defeat.
translations.idiomatic: If they happen to meet the enemy, they immediately suffer defeat.

sentences.zh: 既莫敢折其前鋒，又不能邀其歸路。

translations.literal: They neither dare check the enemy vanguard nor intercept their route of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: They neither dare check the enemy vanguard nor intercept their route of retreat.

sentences.zh: 敵進獲重利，退無後憂，致兵鋒不靖，邊患靡寧。

translations.literal: The enemy advances and gains great profit, retreats without concern for pursuit, causing military unrest and unceasing border troubles.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy advances and gains great profit, retreats without concern for pursuit, and so military unrest persists and border troubles never cease.

sentences.zh: 命將徂征，四年三舉，絕無寸功。

translations.literal: Generals were ordered to campaign; in four years three expeditions were launched, with not a whit of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Generals were ordered to campaign. In four years three expeditions were launched, with not a whit of merit.

sentences.zh: 或高臥而歸，或安行以返。

translations.literal: Some returned after lying high in bed; others came back after an easy march.
translations.idiomatic: Some returned after lying abed; others came back after an easy march.

sentences.zh: 析圭擔爵，優遊朝行，輦帛輿金，充刃私室。

translations.literal: They received jade scepters and carried noble titles, strolling at leisure in the court procession, with silk, coins, and gold filling their private chambers.
translations.idiomatic: They received jade scepters and carried noble titles, strolling at leisure in the court procession, with silk, coins, and gold filling their private chambers.

sentences.zh: 且軍旅一動，輒報捷音，賜予濫施，官秩輕授。

translations.literal: Moreover as soon as troops move, victory is immediately reported; rewards are lavishly bestowed and official ranks lightly granted.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as soon as troops move, victory is immediately reported, rewards are lavishly bestowed, and official ranks are lightly granted.

sentences.zh: 甚至妄殺平民，謬稱首級。

translations.literal: Some even kill civilians without cause and falsely claim them as heads taken.
translations.idiomatic: Some even kill civilians without cause and falsely claim them as heads taken.

sentences.zh: 敵未敗北，輒以奔遁為辭。

translations.literal: When the enemy has not been routed, they cite the enemy's flight as excuse.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy has not been routed, they cite the enemy's flight as excuse.

sentences.zh: 功賞所加，非私家子弟，即權門廝養。

translations.literal: Those receiving merit rewards are either one's own sons and nephews or the menials of powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: Those receiving merit rewards are either one's own sons and nephews or the menials of powerful families.

sentences.zh: 而什伍之卒，轉餉之民，則委骨荒城，膏血野草。

translations.literal: Yet common soldiers and transport corvée laborers leave their bones in desolate fortresses and shed their blood on wild grass.
translations.idiomatic: Yet common soldiers and transport corvée laborers leave their bones in desolate fortresses and shed their blood on wild grass.

sentences.zh: 天怒人怨，禍幾日深，非細故也。

translations.literal: Heaven's anger and men's resentment—disaster grows daily; this is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's anger and men's resentment—disaster grows daily. This is no small matter.

sentences.zh: 京營素號冗怯。

translations.literal: The Capital Garrison has long been known as bloated and cowardly.
translations.idiomatic: The Capital Garrison has long been known as bloated and cowardly.

sentences.zh: 留鎮京師，猶恐未壯根本，顧乃輕於出禦，用褻天威。

translations.literal: Keeping them to guard the capital, one still fears the foundation is not strong enough; yet they are lightly sent out on campaign, debasing imperial majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Keeping them to guard the capital, one still fears the foundation is not strong enough. Yet they are lightly sent out on campaign, debasing imperial majesty.

sentences.zh: 臨陣輒奔，反墮邊軍之功，為敵人所侮。

translations.literal: In battle they flee at once, undermining the border troops' achievements and inviting the enemy's contempt.
translations.idiomatic: In battle they flee at once, undermining the border troops' achievements and inviting the enemy's contempt.

sentences.zh: 且延綏邊也，去京師遠；

translations.literal: Moreover Yan-sui is a border region, far from the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Yan-sui is a border region, far from the capital;

sentences.zh: 宣府、大同亦邊也，去京師近。

translations.literal: Xuanfu and Datong are also border regions, close to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanfu and Datong are also border regions, close to the capital.

sentences.zh: 彼有門庭之喻，此無陛楯之嚴，可乎？

translations.literal: The former has the analogy of gate and courtyard; the latter lacks the strictness of the throne's screen—is this acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: The former has the analogy of gate and courtyard; the latter lacks the strictness of the throne's screen—is this acceptable?

sentences.zh: 頃兵部建議：令宣府出兵五千，大同出兵一萬，並力以援延綏，而不慮其相去既遠，往返不逮，人心苦於轉移，馬力疲於奔軼。

translations.literal: Recently the Ministry of War proposed: order Xuanfu to send five thousand troops and Datong ten thousand, combining strength to relieve Yan-sui, without considering that the distances are already great, that round trips cannot keep pace, that men's hearts suffer from constant transfers, and horses' strength is exhausted by rapid marches.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Ministry of War proposed ordering Xuanfu to send five thousand troops and Datong ten thousand, combining strength to relieve Yan-sui, without considering that the distances are already great, that round trips cannot keep pace, that men's hearts suffer from constant transfers, and that horses' strength is exhausted by rapid marches.

sentences.zh: 夫聲東擊西者，賊寇之奸態也。

translations.literal: Feigning east and striking west is the cunning tactic of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Feigning east and striking west is the cunning tactic of bandits.

sentences.zh: 搗虛批亢者，兵家之長策也。

translations.literal: Striking where the enemy is empty and attacking his vital point is the supreme strategy of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Striking where the enemy is empty and attacking his vital point is the supreme strategy of warfare.

sentences.zh: 精銳既盡乎西，老弱乃留於北。

translations.literal: The elite troops are all exhausted in the west while the old and weak remain in the north.
translations.idiomatic: The elite troops are all exhausted in the west while the old and weak remain in the north.

sentences.zh: 萬一北或有警，而西未可離，首尾衡決，遠近坐困，其可為得計哉？

translations.literal: If perchance there is an alarm in the north while the west cannot be abandoned, the head and tail will be broken apart and near and far will sit trapped—is this a sound plan?
translations.idiomatic: If perchance there is an alarm in the north while the west cannot be abandoned, the head and tail will be broken apart and near and far will sit trapped—is this a sound plan?

sentences.zh: 至於延綏士馬屯集，糧糗不貲，乃以山西、河南之民任飛芻轉粟之役。

translations.literal: As for Yan-sui, where troops and horses are massed and grain stores are insufficient, the people of Shanxi and Henan are made to bear the duties of rapid fodder and grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: As for Yan-sui, where troops and horses are massed and grain stores are insufficient, the people of Shanxi and Henan are made to bear the duties of rapid fodder and grain transport.

sentences.zh: 徒步千里，夫運而妻供，父挽而子荷，道路愁怨，井落空虛。

translations.literal: On foot for a thousand li, husbands transport while wives supply, fathers pull while sons carry; the roads are full of grievance and villages lie empty.
translations.idiomatic: On foot for a thousand li, husbands transport while wives supply, fathers pull while sons carry. The roads are full of grievance and villages lie empty.

sentences.zh: 幸而得至，束芻百錢，鬥粟倍直；

translations.literal: If they luckily arrive, a bundle of fodder costs a hundred cash and a bushel of grain double the normal price;
translations.idiomatic: If they luckily arrive, a bundle of fodder costs a hundred cash and a bushel of grain double the normal price;

sentences.zh: 不幸遇賊，身且斃矣，他尚何雲。

translations.literal: if unluckily they meet bandits, their bodies perish—what else can be said?
translations.idiomatic: if unluckily they meet bandits, their bodies perish—what else can be said?

sentences.zh: 輸將不足則有輕賫，輕賫不足又有預征。

translations.literal: When transport is insufficient there is cash commutation; when cash commutation is insufficient there is advance collection.
translations.idiomatic: When transport is insufficient there is cash commutation; when cash commutation is insufficient there is advance collection.

sentences.zh: 水旱不可先知，豐歉未能逆卜，征如何其可預也。

translations.literal: Flood and drought cannot be foreknown, plenty and shortage cannot be divined in advance—how can collection be made beforehand?
translations.idiomatic: Flood and drought cannot be foreknown, and plenty and shortage cannot be divined in advance—how can collection be made beforehand?

sentences.zh: 又令民輸芻粟補官，而媚權貴私親故者，或出空牒以授，倉庾無升合之入。

translations.literal: Officials were also allowed to substitute for office by submitting fodder and grain; those currying favor with the powerful and favoring private friends sometimes issued empty warrants, and granaries received not a measure of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were also allowed to substitute for office by submitting fodder and grain. Those currying favor with the powerful and favoring private friends sometimes issued empty warrants, and granaries received not a measure of grain.

sentences.zh: 至若輸粟給鹽，則豪右請托，率占虛名鬻之，而商賈費且倍蓰。

translations.literal: As for submitting grain to receive salt certificates, powerful families through patronage mostly monopolized nominal quotas to sell, while merchants paid costs many times over.
translations.idiomatic: As for submitting grain to receive salt certificates, powerful families through patronage mostly monopolized nominal quotas to sell, while merchants paid costs many times over.

sentences.zh: 官爵日輕，鹽法日沮，而邊儲之不充如故也。

translations.literal: Official ranks grew daily cheaper, the salt system daily more obstructed, yet border stores remained as empty as before.
translations.idiomatic: Official ranks grew daily cheaper, the salt system daily more obstructed, yet border stores remained as empty as before.

sentences.zh: 又朝廷出帑藏給邊，歲為銀數十萬。

translations.literal: Moreover the court disbursed from the treasury to supply the borders, tens of thousands of taels of silver each year.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the court disbursed from the treasury to supply the borders, tens of thousands of taels of silver each year.

sentences.zh: 山西、河南輸輕賫於邊者，歲不下數十萬。

translations.literal: Shanxi and Henan sent cash commutation to the borders each year, no less than several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi and Henan sent cash commutation to the borders each year, no less than several hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 銀日積而多則銀益賤，粟日散而少則粟益貴。

translations.literal: As silver accumulated daily and grew abundant, silver grew cheaper; as grain was dispersed daily and grew scarce, grain grew dearer.
translations.idiomatic: As silver accumulated daily and grew abundant, silver grew cheaper; as grain was dispersed daily and grew scarce, grain grew dearer.

sentences.zh: 而不知者，遂於養兵之中，寓養狙之術。

translations.literal: Yet those who did not understand embedded the art of feeding monkeys within the scheme of maintaining troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who did not understand embedded the art of feeding monkeys within the scheme of maintaining troops.

sentences.zh: 或以茶鹽，或以銀布，名為準折糧價，實則侵克軍需。

translations.literal: Sometimes using tea and salt, sometimes silver and cloth, nominally to convert grain prices, but in fact embezzling military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes using tea and salt, sometimes silver and cloth, nominally to convert grain prices, but in fact embezzling military supplies.

sentences.zh: 故朝廷有糜廩之虞，軍士無果腹之樂。

translations.literal: Therefore the court feared depletion of granaries while soldiers had no joy of filling their bellies.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the court feared depletion of granaries while soldiers had no joy of filling their bellies.

sentences.zh: 至兵馬所經，例須應付。

translations.literal: When troops and horses pass through, localities must by regulation supply them.
translations.idiomatic: When troops and horses pass through, localities must by regulation supply them.

sentences.zh: 居平，人日米一斗，馬日芻一束。

translations.literal: In normal times, one person receives one dou of rice per day, one horse one bundle of fodder per day.
translations.idiomatic: In normal times, one person receives one dou of rice per day, and one horse one bundle of fodder per day.

sentences.zh: 追逐，一日之間或一二堡，或三四城，豈能俱給哉？

translations.literal: In pursuit, in a single day one may pass one or two forts or three or four walled cities—how can all be supplied?
translations.idiomatic: In pursuit, in a single day one may pass one or two forts or three or four walled cities—how can all be supplied?

sentences.zh: 而典守者巧為竊攘之謀，凡所經歷悉有開支，罔上行私，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: Yet those in charge craftily scheme for private plunder; wherever they pass there are disbursements recorded—deceiving superiors for private gain, nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those in charge craftily scheme for private plunder. Wherever they pass there are disbursements recorded—deceiving superiors for private gain, nothing exceeds this.

sentences.zh: 及訪禦敵之策，則又論議紛紜。

translations.literal: When seeking strategies for repelling the enemy, discussion was again tangled and confused.
translations.idiomatic: When seeking strategies for repelling the enemy, discussion was again tangled and confused.

sentences.zh: 有謂復受降之故險，守東勝之舊城，使聲援交接，犄角易制。

translations.literal: Some held that one should recover the old strategic position at Shoujiang, hold the former city of Dongsheng, link supporting forces in mutual aid, and coordinate in pincer attack for easy control.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued for recovering the old Shoujiang pass, garrisoning the former city of Dongsheng, linking supporting forces, and coordinating from mutually supporting positions for easier control.

sentences.zh: 夫欲復城河北，即須塞外屯兵。

translations.literal: Now if one wishes to restore cities north of the River, one must station troops beyond the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: To restore cities north of the Yellow River, troops would have to be garrisoned beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 出孤遠之軍，涉荒漠之地，輜重為累，饋餉惟艱。

translations.literal: Sending armies into isolated distance, crossing desert wastes, baggage becomes a burden, and supplying provisions is extremely difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Sending armies into remote isolation across desert wastes makes baggage a burden and resupply extraordinarily difficult.

sentences.zh: 彼或抄掠於前，躡襲於後。

translations.literal: The enemy may raid in front and pursue from behind.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy might raid ahead and harry from the rear.

sentences.zh: 曠日持久，軍食乏絕。

translations.literal: Days stretch into prolonged time, and army provisions run out.
translations.idiomatic: As days drag on, army provisions are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 進不得城，退不得歸，一敗而聲威大損矣。

translations.literal: Advancing they cannot take cities; retreating they cannot return—and one defeat greatly damages renown and authority.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to advance and take cities or retreat in safety, a single defeat would greatly damage the dynasty's prestige.

sentences.zh: 又有謂統十萬之眾，裹半月之糧，奮揚武威，掃蕩窟穴，使河套一空。

translations.literal: Others held that one should command a force of a hundred thousand, carry half a month's provisions, display martial might, sweep clean the lairs, and empty the Ordos entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Others proposed commanding a hundred thousand men with half a month's rations, displaying martial might to sweep the enemy lairs and clear the Ordos entirely.

sentences.zh: 事非不善也。

translations.literal: The plan is not without merit.
translations.idiomatic: This was not a bad plan in itself.

sentences.zh: 然帝王之兵，以全取勝；

translations.literal: Yet the armies of emperors and kings take victory through wholeness and completeness;
translations.idiomatic: Yet an imperial army wins through completeness and restraint;

sentences.zh: 孫、吳之法，以逸待勞。

translations.literal: The methods of Sun and Wu wait with ease for the enemy's exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: The methods of Sun and Wu counsel waiting at ease for the enemy to tire.

sentences.zh: 今欲鼓勇前行，窮搜遠擊，乘危履險，覬萬一之幸。

translations.literal: Now one wishes to drum up courage and advance, search exhaustively and strike far, ride danger and tread peril, hoping for a one-in-ten-thousand chance.
translations.idiomatic: To drum up courage, advance deep, strike far, and court danger in hope of a lucky break—

sentences.zh: 贏糧遠隨則重不及事，提兵深入則孤不可援。

translations.literal: Carrying provisions on one's back to follow far means the burden cannot match the task; leading troops deep means isolation with no rescue.
translations.idiomatic: carrying grain on one's back would burden troops without serving the purpose, while pushing deep would leave the army isolated and beyond rescue.

sentences.zh: 且其間地方千里，無城郭之居，委積之守。

translations.literal: Moreover, within this region the land stretches a thousand li with no walled settlements to dwell in or stored supplies to guard.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the region stretches a thousand li without walled settlements or stored supplies to fall back on.

sentences.zh: 彼或往來遷徙，罷我馳驅。

translations.literal: The enemy may move to and fro and migrate, wearing out our forced marches.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy could simply move about, wearing down our forced marches.

sentences.zh: 我則情見勢屈，為敵所困。

translations.literal: We would then show our hand and our strength would buckle, trapped by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Our hand would be shown and our strength spent, leaving us trapped by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 既失坐勝之機，必蹈覆沒之轍。

translations.literal: Having lost the opportunity to sit and win, one must tread the track of total destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost the chance to win from a position of strength, we would follow the path to total destruction.

sentences.zh: 其最無策者，又欲棄延綏勿守，使兵民息肩，不知一民尺土皆受之祖宗，不可忽也。

translations.literal: The most imprudent plan of all was again to abandon Yansui and cease defending it, letting soldiers and people rest their shoulders—not knowing that every person and every inch of soil are entrusted by the ancestors and cannot be neglected.
translations.idiomatic: The worst proposal of all was to abandon Yansui altogether and let soldiers and civilians rest easy—not realizing that every subject and every inch of soil was entrusted by the ancestors and must not be cast aside.

sentences.zh: 向失東勝，故今日之害萃於延綏，而關陜震動。

translations.literal: Formerly Dongsheng was lost, so today's harm gathers at Yansui and Shaanxi is shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Because Dongsheng was lost, the harm today converges on Yansui and Shaanxi is shaken.

sentences.zh: 今棄延綏，則他日之害鐘於關陜，而京師震動。

translations.literal: If Yansui is now abandoned, then another day's harm will focus on Shaanxi and the capital will be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: If Yansui were abandoned now, the harm would eventually fall on Shaanxi and the capital itself would be shaken.

sentences.zh: 賊愈近而禍愈大矣。

translations.literal: The nearer the bandits, the greater the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The nearer the enemy drew, the greater the disaster would become.

sentences.zh: 因陳重將權、增城堡、廣斥堠、募民壯、去客兵、明賞罰、嚴間諜、實屯田、復邊漕數事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set forth several measures: weighty authority to generals, increasing fortresses and walled cities, extending warning beacons, recruiting sturdy civilians, removing guest troops, clarifying rewards and punishments, tightening espionage, filling in military colonies, and restoring frontier grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore proposed several measures: empowering senior generals, expanding fortifications, extending warning beacons, recruiting local militia, removing outside troops, clarifying rewards and punishments, tightening intelligence work, revitalizing military colonies, and restoring frontier grain transport.

sentences.zh: 時兵部方主用兵，不能盡用也。

translations.literal: At the time the Ministry of War was advocating the use of force and could not fully adopt his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Ministry of War was pushing for military action and could not fully adopt his proposals.

sentences.zh: 十四年十月卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, tenth month, he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of the fourteenth year, at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，謚文毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Junior Guardian and given the posthumous title Wanyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian and given the posthumous title Wanyi ("cultured and resolute").

sentences.zh: 明世父子官翰林，俱謚文，自嶽始。

translations.literal: In the Ming dynasty, father and son serving as Hanlin officials both received posthumous titles with "Wen," beginning with Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ming, when father and son both served in the Hanlin Academy and both received posthumous titles containing "Wen," Yue was the first such case.

sentences.zh: 閔珪，字朝瑛，烏程人。

translations.literal: Min Gui, styled Zhaoying, was a native of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Min Gui, styled Zhaoying, came from Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 天順八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the eighth year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 出按河南，以風力聞。

translations.literal: Dispatched to inspect Henan, he became known for his forceful integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to inspect Henan, he became known for his forceful integrity.

sentences.zh: 成化六年擢江西副使，進廣東按察使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chenghua he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi and advanced to Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Chenghua he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi and then to Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 久之，以右僉都御史巡撫江西。

translations.literal: After some time he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 南、贛諸府多盜，率強宗家仆。

translations.literal: The prefectures of Nan and Gan had many bandits, mostly retainers of powerful clans.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures of Nan and Gan had many bandits, mostly drawn from the retainers of powerful clans.

sentences.zh: 珪請獲盜連坐其主，法司議從之。

translations.literal: Gui requested that captured bandits entail punishment of their masters by association; the judicial offices deliberated and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Gui proposed that captured bandits bring their masters to account through collective punishment; the judicial offices agreed.

sentences.zh: 尹直輩謀之李孜省，取中旨責珪不能弭盜，左遷廣西按察使。

translations.literal: Yin Zhi and his associates plotted with Li Zisheng, obtained a secret edict rebuking Gui for failing to quell banditry, and demoted him to Surveillance Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhi and his associates plotted with Li Zisheng, secured a secret edict rebuking Gui for failing to suppress banditry, and had him demoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，擢右副都御史，巡撫順天。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, Gui was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiaozong Emperor succeeded to the throne, Gui was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 入為刑部右侍郎，進右都御史，總督兩廣軍務，與總兵官毛銳討古田僮。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of Punishments, advanced to Right Censor-in-Chief, and as supreme commander of the two Guang circuits joined Commander-in-Chief Mao Rui in campaigning against the Yao of Gutian.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of Punishments, rose to Right Censor-in-Chief, and as supreme commander of Guangdong and Guangxi joined Commander-in-Chief Mao Rui in campaigning against the Yao of Gutian.

sentences.zh: 副總兵馬俊、參議馬鉉自臨桂深入，敗死，軍遂退。

translations.literal: Vice Commander Ma Jun and Assistant Commissioner Ma Xuan advanced deep from Lingui; they were defeated and killed, and the army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Ma Jun and Assistant Commissioner Ma Xuan pressed deep from Lingui, were defeated and killed, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔停俸討賊。

translations.literal: An edict ordered suspension of salary until the bandits were suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that their salaries be suspended until the bandits were suppressed.

sentences.zh: 珪復進兵，連破七寨，他賊悉就撫。

translations.literal: Gui again advanced troops, successively stormed seven stockades, and the other bandits all submitted to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Gui resumed the offensive, captured seven stockades in succession, and the remaining bandits all submitted.

sentences.zh: 弘治七年遷南京刑部尚書，尋召為左都御史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Hongzhi he was transferred to Minister of Punishments at Nanjing; soon after he was summoned as Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Hongzhi he was transferred to Minister of Punishments at Nanjing and soon summoned back as Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十一年，東宮出閣，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the Eastern Palace left the inner quarters, he was added Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when the crown prince left the inner quarters, Gui was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年代白昂為刑部尚書，再加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he replaced Bai Ang as Minister of Punishments and was further given Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he replaced Bai Ang as Minister of Punishments and was further made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以災異與都御史戴珊共陳時政八事，又陳刑獄四事，多報可。

translations.literal: On account of calamities and omens he jointly with Censor-in-Chief Dai Shan set forth eight matters of current policy, and again set forth four matters concerning criminal justice; most were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Following calamities and portents, he and Censor-in-Chief Dai Shan jointly submitted eight proposals on current policy and four on the administration of justice; most were approved.

sentences.zh: 珪久為法官，議獄皆會情比律，歸於仁恕。

translations.literal: Gui had long served as a judicial official; in deliberating cases he always matched circumstances to the law and leaned toward clemency.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had long served as a judicial official. In deliberating cases he matched circumstances to the law and leaned toward clemency.

sentences.zh: 宣府妖人李道明聚眾燒香，巡撫劉聰信千戶黃珍言，株連數十家，謂道明將引北寇攻宣府。

translations.literal: At Xuanfu the sorcerer Li Daoming gathered a crowd to burn incense; Grand Coordinator Liu Cong believed the words of Battalion Commander Huang Zhen, implicated dozens of households, and claimed Daoming would lead northern raiders to attack Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuanfu the sorcerer Li Daoming gathered followers to burn incense. Grand Coordinator Liu Cong believed Battalion Commander Huang Zhen and implicated dozens of households, claiming Daoming would lead northern raiders against Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 及逮訊無驗，珪乃止坐道明一人，余悉得釋，而抵珍罪，聰亦下獄貶官。

translations.literal: When arrest and interrogation yielded no proof, Gui then punished only Daoming alone; the rest were all released, Zhen was held liable for his crime, and Cong was also imprisoned and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: When arrest and interrogation found no proof, Gui punished only Daoming; the rest were released, Zhen was held accountable, and Cong was imprisoned and demoted.

sentences.zh: 帝之親鞫吳一貫也，將置大辟，珪進曰：「一貫推案不實，罪當徒。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor personally tried Wu Yiguan and was about to impose capital punishment, Gui stepped forward and said, "Yiguan's forced confession of an unsound case merits banishment, not death.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor personally tried Wu Yiguan and was about to impose the death penalty, Gui stepped forward: "Yiguan's forced confession on an unsound case warrants banishment, not death.

sentences.zh: 帝不允，珪執如初。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not agree; Gui held to his original opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor refused; Gui held firm to his original view.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，戴珊從旁解之。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew angry; Dai Shan interceded from the side.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grew angry, and Dai Shan interceded from the side.

sentences.zh: 帝乃霽威，令更擬。

translations.literal: The Emperor then cleared his wrath and ordered a new proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's anger abated, and he ordered a new proposal.

sentences.zh: 珪終以原擬上，帝不悅，召語劉大夏。

translations.literal: Gui ultimately submitted the original proposal; the Emperor was displeased and summoned Liu Daxia to speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui ultimately submitted his original proposal. The Emperor was displeased and summoned Liu Daxia for counsel.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「刑官執法乃其職，未可深罪。」

translations.literal: Liu replied, "For a judicial official to uphold the law is his duty; he cannot be deeply faulted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu replied: "For a judicial official to uphold the law is his duty; he ought not be heavily punished.

sentences.zh: 帝默然久之，曰：「朕亦知珪老成不易得，但此事太執耳。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was silent for a long time, then said, "I also know that Gui is experienced and not easily replaced, but on this matter he is too stubborn."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was silent a long while, then said: "I know Gui is experienced and not easily replaced, but on this matter he is too stubborn."

sentences.zh: 卒如珪議。

translations.literal: In the end the judgment followed Gui's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the sentence followed Gui's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 正德元年六月，以年逾七十再疏求退，不允。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Zhengde, having passed seventy he again submitted a memorial requesting retirement, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of Zhengde, having passed seventy he again requested retirement, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 及劉瑾用事，九卿伏闕固諫，韓文被斥，珪復連章乞休。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin came to power, the Nine Ministers knelt at the palace gate in firm remonstrance; Han Wen was dismissed, and Gui again submitted successive memorials requesting leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin came to power, the Nine Ministers knelt at the palace gate in firm remonstrance. Han Wen was dismissed, and Gui again submitted successive memorials requesting retirement.

sentences.zh: 明年二月詔加少保，賜敕馳傳歸。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year an edict added Junior Guardian and granted an imperial commission to return home by relay horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year an edict made him Junior Guardian and granted an imperial commission for his return home by relay horse.

sentences.zh: 六年十月卒，年八十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, tenth month, he died, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of the sixth year, at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，謚莊懿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Senior Guardian and given the posthumous title Zhuangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Senior Guardian and given the posthumous title Zhuangyi ("dignified and virtuous").

sentences.zh: 從孫如霖，南京禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His grand-nephew Rulin was Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His grand-nephew Rulin served as Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 如霖曾孫洪學，吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Rulin's great-grandson Hongxue was Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Rulin's great-grandson Hongxue served as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 洪學從弟夢得，兵部戎政尚書。

translations.literal: Hongxue's cousin Mengde was Minister of War for Frontier Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxue's cousin Mengde served as Minister of War for Frontier Affairs.

sentences.zh: 他為庶僚者復數人。

translations.literal: Others among them served as ordinary officials, several more in number.
translations.idiomatic: Several others of the family also served as ordinary officials.

sentences.zh: 戴珊，字廷珍，浮梁人。

translations.literal: Dai Shan, styled Tingzhen, was a native of Fuliang.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Shan, styled Tingzhen, came from Fuliang.

sentences.zh: 父哻，由鄉舉官嘉興教授，有學行。

translations.literal: His father Bei passed the provincial examination and served as Director of Studies at Jiaxing; he had learning and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bei passed the provincial examination and served as Director of Studies at Jiaxing; he was a man of learning and integrity.

sentences.zh: 富人數輩遣其奴子入學，哻不可。

translations.literal: Several wealthy men sent their slave sons to enter the school; Bei would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Several wealthy men tried to enroll their slave sons; Bei refused.

sentences.zh: 賄上官強之，執愈堅，見忤，坐他事去。

translations.literal: They bribed superiors to force the matter; Bei held all the more firmly, gave offense, and was removed on another charge.
translations.idiomatic: They bribed his superiors to force the issue, but Bei held firm, gave offense, and was removed on another charge.

sentences.zh: 珊幼嗜學，天順末，與劉大夏同舉進士。

translations.literal: Shan from youth loved learning; at the end of Tianshun he passed the jinshi together with Liu Daxia.
translations.idiomatic: Shan loved learning from youth. At the end of the Tianshun reign he passed the jinshi together with Liu Daxia.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢御史，督南畿學政。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to investigating censor and supervised educational policy in the Southern Metropolitan Region.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to investigating censor and placed in charge of educational policy in the Southern Metropolitan Region.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年遷陜西副使，仍督學政。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chenghua he was transferred to Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi while still supervising educational policy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Chenghua he was transferred to Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi while continuing to supervise educational policy.

sentences.zh: 正身率教，士皆愛慕之。

translations.literal: He corrected his own person and led in teaching; scholars all loved and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: He led by personal example in teaching, and scholars admired him.

sentences.zh: 歷浙江按察使，福建左、右布政使，終任不攜一土物。

translations.literal: He served successively as Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang and Left and Right Provincial Commissioner of Fujian; at the end of each term he carried away not a single local product.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang and Left and Right Provincial Commissioner of Fujian; at the end of each posting he took away not a single local product.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年，以王恕薦擢右副都御史，撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi, on Wang Shu's recommendation he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and pacification commissioner of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Hongzhi, on Wang Shu's recommendation he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed pacification commissioner of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 蜀盜野王剛流劫竹山、平利。

translations.literal: The Shu bandit Ye Wanggang roved and plundered Zhushan and Pingli.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu bandit Ye Wanggang roved through Zhushan and Pingli, plundering as he went.

sentences.zh: 珊合川、陜兵，檄副使朱漢等討擒其魁，余皆以脅從論，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Shan combined troops from Sichuan and Shaanxi, issued orders to Vice Commissioner Zhu Han and others to campaign and capture the ringleader; the rest were all judged as coerced followers, sparing many lives.
translations.idiomatic: Shan combined troops from Sichuan and Shaanxi and dispatched Vice Commissioner Zhu Han and others to capture the ringleader; the rest were treated as coerced followers, sparing many lives.

sentences.zh: 入歷刑部左、右侍郎，與尚書何喬新、彭韶共事。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and served successively as Left and Right Vice Minister of Punishments, working together with Ministers He Qiaoxin and Peng Shao.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital and served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Punishments, working with Ministers He Qiaoxin and Peng Shao.

sentences.zh: 晉府寧化王鐘鈵淫虐不孝，勘不得實，再遣珊等勘之，遂奪爵禁錮。

translations.literal: Zhong Min of the Prince of Jin's Ninghua line was licentious, cruel, and unfilial; investigation could not establish the facts, so Shan and others were again dispatched to investigate; the title was then stripped and he was confined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Min, a prince of the Jin line in Ninghua, was licentious, cruel, and unfilial. An initial investigation failed to establish the facts, so Shan and others were sent again; the title was stripped and he was confined.

sentences.zh: 進南京刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He advanced to Minister of Punishments at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Punishments at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 久之，召為左都御史。

translations.literal: After some time he was summoned as Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was summoned back as Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十七年，考察京官，珊廉介不茍合。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, during the inspection of capital officials, Shan was incorruptible and uncompromising.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, during the inspection of capital officials, Shan was incorruptible and would not compromise.

sentences.zh: 給事中吳、王蓋自疑見黜，連疏詆吏部尚書馬文升，並言珊縱妻子納賄。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Wu and Wang Gai, suspecting they would be dismissed, submitted successive memorials slandering Minister of Personnel Ma Wensheng and also saying Shan let his wife and children accept bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Wu and Wang Gai, fearing dismissal, submitted successive memorials attacking Minister of Personnel Ma Wensheng and accusing Shan of letting his wife and children accept bribes.

sentences.zh: 珊等乞罷，帝慰留之。
