translations.literal: Shan and the others requested dismissal; the Emperor comforted them and kept them in office.
translations.idiomatic: Shan and the others asked to resign; the Emperor comforted them and kept them in post.

sentences.zh: 御史馮允中等言：「文升、珊歷事累朝，清德素著，不可因浮詞廢計典。」

translations.literal: Censor Feng Yunzhong and others said, "Wensheng and Shan have served through many reigns with clear virtue long established; they cannot be removed from the inspection roster because of loose words.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Feng Yunzhong and others said: "Wensheng and Shan have served through many reigns with established reputations for integrity; they cannot be removed from the inspection roster on loose talk alone.

sentences.zh: 乃下、蓋詔獄，命文升、珊即舉察事。

translations.literal: Wu and Gai were sent to the imperial prison by edict, and Wensheng and Shan were ordered to proceed with the inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Gai were imprisoned by imperial edict, and Wensheng and Shan were ordered to proceed with the inspection.

sentences.zh: 珊等言：「兩人逆計當黜，故先劾臣等。

translations.literal: Shan and the others said, "The two of them anticipated they would be dismissed, so they first impeached us.
translations.idiomatic: Shan and the others said: "The two men anticipated dismissal and so impeached us first.

sentences.zh: 今黜之，彼必曰是挾私也。

translations.literal: If they are now dismissed, they will surely say it is personal retaliation.
translations.idiomatic: If we dismiss them now, they will surely claim it is personal retaliation.

sentences.zh: 茍避不黜，則負委任，而使詐諼者得誌。」

translations.literal: If one avoids dismissing them out of caution, then one fails the trust assigned and lets deceivers achieve their aim.
translations.idiomatic: If we spare them to avoid that appearance, we fail our charge and let deceivers triumph.

sentences.zh: 帝命上兩人事跡，皆黜之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the records of the two submitted; both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered their records submitted; both were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 已，劉健等因召對，力言蓋罪輕，宜調用。

translations.literal: Afterwards Liu Jian and others, taking advantage of an imperial audience, strongly argued that Gai's offense was light and he should be transferred and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Jian and others, at an imperial audience, argued strongly that Gai's offense was minor and he should be transferred rather than dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝方向用文升、珊，卒不納。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then inclined to employ Wensheng and Shan and ultimately did not accept the suggestion.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was then set on keeping Wensheng and Shan and did not accept the suggestion.

sentences.zh: 帝晚年召對大臣，珊與大夏造膝宴見尤數。

translations.literal: In the Emperor's later years he summoned great ministers for audience; Shan and Daxia enjoyed especially frequent intimate feasts and meetings knee to knee.
translations.idiomatic: In the Emperor's later years he summoned senior ministers for audience; Shan and Daxia were especially often received at intimate audiences.

sentences.zh: 一日，與大夏侍坐。

translations.literal: One day he and Daxia attended seated beside the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: One day Shan and Daxia were in attendance.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「時當述職，諸大臣皆杜門。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "It is time for reporting duties; all the great ministers keep their doors closed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "It is time for the annual reporting of duties, yet most ministers keep their doors shut.

sentences.zh: 如二卿者，雖日見客何害。」

translations.literal: For ministers such as you two, what harm if you receive guests daily?
translations.idiomatic: Ministers such as you two—what harm if you receive guests every day?

sentences.zh: 袖出白金賚之，曰：「少佐而廉。」

translations.literal: He drew silver from his sleeve and bestowed it, saying, "A little to supplement your integrity."
translations.idiomatic: He drew silver from his sleeve and bestowed it, saying: "A little something to supplement your modest means."

sentences.zh: 且屬勿廷謝，曰：「恐為他人忌也。」

translations.literal: And he instructed them not to thank him at court, saying, "I fear others would be jealous."
translations.idiomatic: He added that they should not thank him at court: "I fear others would grow jealous."

sentences.zh: 珊以老疾數求退，輒優詔勉留，遣醫賜食，慰諭有加。

translations.literal: Shan repeatedly requested retirement on account of age and illness; each time a gracious edict urged him to remain, physicians were dispatched, food was bestowed, and consolation and encouragement were heaped upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Shan repeatedly sought retirement on grounds of age and illness; each time the Emperor sent a gracious edict urging him to stay, dispatched physicians, bestowed food, and heaped encouragement upon him.

sentences.zh: 珊感激泣下，私語大夏曰：「珊老病子幼，恐一旦先朝露，公同年好友，何惜一言乎？」

translations.literal: Shan, moved to tears, spoke privately to Daxia, "Shan is old and ill with young sons; I fear I may one day depart before the morning dew dries—you and I are friends of the same graduating year; would you spare a word?
translations.idiomatic: Moved to tears, Shan spoke privately to Daxia: "I am old and ill with young sons; I fear I may die at any moment—you are my friend from the same graduating year; would you not speak a word on my behalf?

sentences.zh: 大夏曰：「唯唯。」

translations.literal: Daxia said, "Yes, yes."
translations.idiomatic: Daxia said: "Yes, yes."

sentences.zh: 後大夏燕對畢，帝問珊病狀，言珊實病，乞憫憐聽其歸。

translations.literal: Later, when Daxia's informal audience ended, the Emperor asked about Shan's illness; Daxia said Shan was truly ill and begged compassion to let him retire.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after an informal audience, the Emperor asked after Shan's health; Daxia said Shan was truly ill and begged the Emperor to show compassion and allow him to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「彼屬卿言耶？

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Did that come from your advice?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Was that your counsel?

sentences.zh: 主人留客堅，客則強留。

translations.literal: When the host presses a guest to stay, the guest should press to stay in turn.
translations.idiomatic: When a host presses a guest to stay, the guest in turn should press to remain.

sentences.zh: 珊獨不能為朕留耶？

translations.literal: Can Shan alone not stay for Us?
translations.idiomatic: Can Shan alone not stay on for me?

sentences.zh: 且朕以天下事付卿輩，猶家人父子。

translations.literal: Moreover We entrust the affairs of All-under-Heaven to you ministers as to family between father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I entrust the affairs of the realm to you ministers as one entrusts them to one's own family, father and son together.

sentences.zh: 今太平未兆，何忍言歸！」

translations.literal: Now the signs of great peace have not yet appeared—how can you bear to speak of returning home!
translations.idiomatic: Great peace has not yet dawned—how can you bear to speak of going home!

sentences.zh: 大夏出以告珊，珊泣曰：「臣死是官矣。」

translations.literal: Daxia went out and told Shan; Shan wept and said, "Your servant will die in this office."
translations.idiomatic: Daxia went out and told Shan; Shan wept and said, "I shall die in this office."

sentences.zh: 帝既崩，珊以新君嗣位不忍言去，力疾視事。

translations.literal: After the Emperor died, Shan, because the new ruler had just succeeded, could not bear to speak of leaving and forced himself to attend to duties despite illness.
translations.idiomatic: After the Emperor died, Shan, with the new ruler just ascended, could not bear to speak of leaving and forced himself to carry on despite illness.

sentences.zh: 疾作，遂卒。

translations.literal: His illness took hold and he thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: His illness took hold and he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚恭簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Gongjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Gongjian.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：孝宗之為明賢君，有以哉。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: That Xiaozong was a worthy ruler of Ming had its reasons.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser says: That Xiaozong was a worthy ruler of the Ming had good reason.

sentences.zh: 恭儉自飭，而明於任人。

translations.literal: He was respectful and frugal in self-discipline and clear-sighted in appointing men.
translations.idiomatic: He was respectful and frugal in his own conduct and clear-sighted in appointing men.

sentences.zh: 劉、謝諸賢居政府，而王恕、何喬新、彭韶等為七卿長，相與維持而匡弼之。

translations.literal: Liu, Xie, and other worthies held the government, while Wang Shu, He Qiaoxin, Peng Shao, and others headed the six ministries, together sustaining and correcting him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, Xie, and other worthies held the government, while Wang Shu, He Qiaoxin, Peng Shao, and others headed the six ministries, together sustaining and correcting him.

sentences.zh: 朝多君子，殆比隆開元、慶歷盛時矣。

translations.literal: The court had many gentlemen; it nearly matched the flourishing age of Kaiyuan and the prosperity of Qingli.
translations.idiomatic: The court abounded in gentlemen; it nearly matched the flourishing age of Kaiyuan and the prosperity of Qingli.

sentences.zh: 喬新、韶雖未究其用，而望著朝野。

translations.literal: Qiaoxin and Shao, though their talents were not fully used, had reputations renowned in court and country.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaoxin and Shao, though their talents were not fully used to the end, enjoyed reputations renowned throughout court and country.

sentences.zh: 史稱宋仁宗時，國未嘗無嬖幸，而不足以累治世之體；

translations.literal: Histories say that in the time of Song Renzong the state was not without favourites, yet they were insufficient to burden the substance of a well-governed age;
translations.idiomatic: Histories say that under Song Renzong the state was not without favourites, yet they were not enough to burden the substance of a well-governed age;

sentences.zh: 朝未嘗無小人，而不足以勝善類之氣。

translations.literal: the court was not without petty men, yet they were insufficient to overcome the spirit of the good.
translations.idiomatic: the court was not without petty men, yet they could not overcome the spirit of the good.

sentences.zh: 孝宗初政，亦略似之。

translations.literal: Xiaozong's early government also resembled this in outline.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong's early government resembled this in outline as well.

sentences.zh: 不然，承憲宗之季，而欲使政不旁撓，財無濫費，滋培元氣，中外乂安，豈易言哉。

translations.literal: Otherwise, succeeding the late years of Xianzong, to wish that government not be diverted aside, wealth not be squandered, vital energy be nourished and strengthened, and inner and outer realms be at peace—how could this be lightly spoken of?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, inheriting the late years of Xianzong, to expect government undiverted, expenditure unreckless, vital energy nourished, and peace within and without—how easily could that be said?
